source_note: This lab explicitly compares a switchboard that keeps lifecycle reward updates with one that observes the same rewards but freezes its action-reward memory. Both policies start from the same stale idle-favoring reward memory: the frozen policy locks into idle in the curious-mood band, while the feedback policy corrects the idle mean from observed lifecycle rewards and resumes active care.

decision.reason: Lifecycle reward feedback corrects a stale idle-favoring action memory and strictly improves need balance over the frozen baseline without reducing survival in this Stage 0 scenario.

limitations: The reward function is still synthetic and hand-authored.
The scenario starts from a deliberately stale idle-favoring reward memory; the advantage is specific to miscalibrations the bandit thread can act on.
The bandit thread's utility contribution is capped at +/-0.125 * confidence, so mood-heuristic-favored miscalibrations (for example stale play rewards) remain undetectable in this architecture.
The lifecycle reward is dominated by the global need balance, which limits how sharply the learner can differentiate action quality.
No persisted online learner state is promoted into packages yet.
No human non-annoyance or attachment rating is included.
